subject: Mosaic Analytics - sudden p99 regressions in extended-context requests
messages:
From: Elaine Kim <ops@mosaic-analytics.com>

Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: High p99 on extended context calls — urgent

Jonas / Laura,

We started seeing a sharp rise in p99 latency and a few 500/429 errors on our production calls that use the 16k context window. This started around 07:40 PDT and has persisted. High-level numbers from our observability:
- baseline (last week) p95 ~ 230ms, p99 ~ 630ms
- spike observed: p95 ~ 270ms, p99 ~ 2.3s (several 3s+ outliers)
- error rate: 0.05% -> 0.9% (mix of 500 and 429 throttles)

We are attaching one representative request payload (request_sample_16k.json) and a small log snippet (error_snapshot.log.txt). Our customers are seeing degraded UX — this is impacting an A/B experiment that's live.

Can Redwood provide an immediate mitigation and timeline for a fix? We need either a fast routing fallback (route long-context requests to any stable pool) or an emergency rollback to the prior model variant. Also please confirm if this qualifies for SLA credits. We can be available for a call now.

Thanks,
Elaine Kim

Subject: Re: High p99 on extended context calls — urgent

Triage summary (initial):
- Observed increased queue depth and slower tail latency from a subset of GPU workers (hosts pool: gfx-us-west-3-a12).
- KV cache hit-rate for Mosaic's tenant dropped ~60% during the window; causes larger memory churn on quantized kernels for long KV sequences (16k).
- We also see increased retry responses from an upstream rate-limiter at the routing layer (429s) when queue depth crosses threshold.

Evidence attached: error_snapshot.log.txt (sample stack traces + timestamps). I pulled the request sample and reproduced a p99 regression in our preprod harness when simulating similar sequence lengths.

Immediate mitigation options (short-lived):
- Route Mosaic long-context traffic to dedicated pool with larger memory headroom (requires provisioning but can be done within 20–45 minutes if capacity available).
- Enable routing fallback to the 8k-compatible model variant for requests over 12k tokens (fastest to flip; ~5–10 minutes).
- Temporarily increase per-tenant concurrency cap for Mosaic to reduce rate-limiter throttling while we stabilize (requires Ops approval).

I recommend enabling the routing fallback to 8k-compatible variant as the fastest mitigation while we perform deeper root cause (kernel selection + memory fragmentation).

Marcus
SRE Lead, Redwood Serving
marcus.lin@redwood.com

Subject: Post-update: Mosaic long-window incident and next steps

Quick summary and outcomes for the internal thread:
- Mitigation executed: routing fallback to 8k-compatible model variant was enabled at 2027-08-03T12:27:00-07:00. Mosaic confirmed p99 returned to baseline by ~12:45 PDT. Metrics attached (metrics_p95_p99_chart.png).
- Root-cause (hypothesis): transient KV cache fragmentation and suboptimal kernel selection when handling sustained 16k windows on a subset of hosts; interacting with routing rate-limiter produced increased 429s.
- Immediate actions assigned:
  - SRE (Marcus): run extended repro and produce kernel-selection trace + memory timeline (ETA 48 hours).
  - Serving/Product: implement a routing policy to prefer dedicated pools for sustained long-window tenants and accelerate kernel selection improvements (ETA: prioritize this sprint).
  - Customer/Account: Laura to schedule exec call with Mosaic (Elaine + Mosaic Eng director) for tomorrow 10:00 PDT and to draft a goodwill credit (suggestion: 10% invoice credit for the impacted month).

Sergio and I will prepare an executive note if needed. Good work on the quick mitigation. We'll follow up with a postmortem and itemized remediation plan.
